claim: Leti syllable structure strongly favors onsets and avoids tautosyllabic consonant clusters; these restrictions actively condition phrase-medial metathesis.

requirements: tautosyllabic consonant clusters avoided/prohibited in the analysis

exceptions_or_counterexamples: Some phrase-initial consonant clusters surface when their sonority profile is acceptable; epenthesis and consonant deletion are reported as unavailable general repairs, so cluster avoidance is not a blanket ban on every surface CC sequence.
section: Introduction; 2 Phrase-medial metathesis; 2.1 Avoidance of complex syllable margins

claim: Phonological phrases are vowel-final: consonant-final morpheme forms undergo final CV metathesis phrase-finally so that the right edge of the phrase is aligned with a vowel.

source_forms.formal_constraint: ALIGN-PHRASE: right edge of P-Phrase aligned with vowel

normalized_environment: final VC -> CV / __ ]P-Phrase to ensure vowel-final phrase
scope: phrase-final forms; phrasing determined by syntax and morphology
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Phrase-medial cognate forms can remain consonant-final before a simple onset; the restriction is explicitly phrasal, not a lexical ban on consonant-final morphemes.

claim: Phrase-medial metathesis is conditioned by the following morpheme shape: before an initial consonant cluster it prevents a complex syllable margin, while before a /CVV/-initial sequence it helps avoid onsetless syllables.

source_forms.repairs: transpose final consonant and vowel of preceding morpheme, with associated resyllabification

normalized_environment: final VC metathesis / __ +CC or __ +CVV, motivated by *COMPLEX/ONSET
exceptions_or_counterexamples: When the following vowel is also high, the first high vowel may delete instead; before a simple onset, phrase-medial forms need not show the same metathesis. The process therefore has explicit segmental and structural conditioning.
section: 2 Phrase-medial metathesis; 2.1 Avoidance of complex syllable margins

claim: The analysis reports a general prohibition against tautosyllabic sequences of high vowels: where phrase-medial restructuring would place one high vowel before another high vowel, the first high vowel deletes rather than yielding the otherwise expected sequence.

source_forms.generalization: first high vowel deletes when following vowel is also high

normalized_environment: avoid tautosyllabic [+high][+high]; first high V deletion in relevant derived configuration
scope: phrase-medial derived forms; linked to Hume 1997 analysis
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The paper refers readers to Hume 1997 for fuller analysis; the present paper gives the prohibition and representative derivations but not an exhaustive lexical exception survey.
